# ModelBatch

Namespace `Nfty.Model` in assembly `Nfty.Model`.

```csharp
public static class ModelBatch
```

Rises many pictures at once and delivers the files to a folder or a zip.

### Export(IReadOnlyList&lt;string&gt;, Func&lt;int, ModelInput&gt;, Action&lt;ModelInput&gt;?, RiseOptions, ModelDestination, IProgress&lt;int&gt;?, CancellationToken, Action&lt;string&gt;?) { #m-export-system-collections-generic-ireadonlylist-system-3ebcb1 }

```csharp
public static ModelExportResult Export(IReadOnlyList<string> baseNames, Func<int, ModelInput> open, Action<ModelInput>? release, RiseOptions options, ModelDestination destination, IProgress<int>? progress = null, CancellationToken cancellation = default, Action<string>? onWritten = null);
```

Rises a batch and writes it as it goes: each model is built, written and let go before the next picture is asked for, so a batch of ten thousand holds one model, never ten thousand.

**Parameters**

- `baseNames` (`IReadOnlyList<string>`) - One wanted name per picture; made safe and distinct exactly as [`ModelBatch.Build()`](Nfty.Model.ModelBatch.md#m-build-system-collections-generic-ienumerable-nfty-mode-3e2a5f) does, in this order.
- `open` (`Func<int, ModelInput>`) - Hands over picture `i`. Called once per index, on the calling thread, never before the previous picture has been released. Its [`ModelInput.BaseName`](Nfty.Model.ModelInput.md#p-basename) is ignored: the name is `baseNames`'s.
- `release` (`Action<ModelInput>?`) - Called once for every opened picture as soon as its files are written (or its build failed); null when the caller keeps ownership.
- `options` (`RiseOptions`) - How to rise and write.
- `destination` (`ModelDestination`) - A folder or a zip.
- `progress` (`IProgress<int>?`) - Told how many pictures are done (written or skipped) after each one.
- `cancellation` (`CancellationToken`) - Checked before each picture. A canceled zip is never left behind (it is written beside its destination and moved over it only when complete); a canceled folder keeps the models finished before the stop, each whole, since a file is written only once its model is.
- `onWritten` (`Action<string>?`) - Told each file's name once it is in the destination, on the thread doing the export; how a caller knows whether a stopped batch wrote anything.

**Returns.** The file names written, the pictures skipped, and the files that already existed.

**Remarks**

Models are written in ordinal order of their first file name, each model's files in the writer's order: for a one-file format that is exactly ordinal order of every entry, so a zip has the bytes [`ModelBatch.WriteZip()`](Nfty.Model.ModelBatch.md#m-writezip-system-string-system-collections-generic-irea-a9168e) would give the built files. Identical input gives identical bytes either way.

### Export(IReadOnlyList&lt;string&gt;, Func&lt;int, ModelInput&gt;, Action&lt;ModelInput&gt;?, RiseOptions, ModelDestination, Parallelism, IProgress&lt;int&gt;?, CancellationToken, Action&lt;string&gt;?) { #m-export-system-collections-generic-ireadonlylist-system-f11170 }

```csharp
public static ModelExportResult Export(IReadOnlyList<string> baseNames, Func<int, ModelInput> open, Action<ModelInput>? release, RiseOptions options, ModelDestination destination, Parallelism parallelism, IProgress<int>? progress = null, CancellationToken cancellation = default, Action<string>? onWritten = null);
```

Rises a batch like [`ModelBatch.Export()`](Nfty.Model.ModelBatch.md#m-export-system-collections-generic-ireadonlylist-system-3ebcb1), but builds meshes in a bounded window of pictures at once and writes them strictly in ordinal order, so the destination holds exactly the bytes the sequential overload gives.

**Parameters**

- `baseNames` (`IReadOnlyList<string>`) - One wanted name per picture; made safe and distinct exactly as [`ModelBatch.Build()`](Nfty.Model.ModelBatch.md#m-build-system-collections-generic-ienumerable-nfty-mode-3e2a5f) does, in this order.
- `open` (`Func<int, ModelInput>`) - Hands over picture `i`. **Called from worker threads**, possibly several at once and for several different pictures: it must be safe to call concurrently. Each picture is released before the batch asks for one beyond the window. Its [`ModelInput.BaseName`](Nfty.Model.ModelInput.md#p-basename) is ignored: the name is `baseNames`'s.
- `release` (`Action<ModelInput>?`) - Called once for every opened picture as soon as its model is built (or its build failed), on the thread that built it; null when the caller keeps ownership.
- `options` (`RiseOptions`) - How to rise and write.
- `destination` (`ModelDestination`) - A folder or a zip.
- `parallelism` (`Parallelism`) - How many pictures build at once. A sequential degree gives exactly the sequential overload's behavior, on the calling thread.
- `progress` (`IProgress<int>?`) - Told how many pictures are done (written or skipped), in order, one call at a time.
- `cancellation` (`CancellationToken`) - Checked before each window and each picture. A canceled zip is never left behind; a canceled folder keeps every model written before the stop, each one whole.
- `onWritten` (`Action<string>?`) - Told each file's name once it is in the destination, in write order, on the calling thread.

**Returns.** The file names written, the pictures skipped, and the files that already existed.

**Remarks**

**Build wide, write narrow.** The mesh build and the file encode are pure functions of one picture and fan out into slots; the sink (a zip's entries share one stream) is only ever touched by the calling thread, in the ordinal order the sequential overload uses. Memory is bounded by the window — at most twice the degree of finished models wait to be written.

When several pictures in one window fail, the lowest-ordinal one is rethrown, so the message never depends on the thread count. A window that fails writes nothing of itself.

Makes a name safe as a file name on every platform.

**Parameters**

**Returns.** The name with reserved and control characters replaced by `-`, outer spaces and dots trimmed; `model` when nothing is left.
